pages.content:
# Welcome to the UUSIVC 2026 Challenge

Welcome to the **Universal UltraSound Image & Video Analysis Challenge 2026: Multi-Organ Classification and Segmentation Across B-mode and Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound**.

This challenge focuses on evaluating algorithms for multi-organ, multi-modal ultrasound image and video analysis. The benchmark covers classification and segmentation tasks across B-mode ultrasound images, contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) videos, and cardiac ultrasound videos. The goal is to advance the generalizability, robustness, and clinical applicability of AI models in ultrasound image analysis.

🧪Participants will benchmark their methods via Codabench through automated submission and evaluation pipelines, with live leaderboards tracking performance across classification and segmentation tasks.

🏆Challenge results and winners will be announced during the [Deep-Breath 2026: 3rd Deep Breast Workshop on AI and Imaging for Diagnostic and Treatment Challenges in Breast Care Workshop](https://deep-breath-miccai.github.io/deepbreath-2026/), held in conjunction with [MICCAI 2026](https://conferences.miccai.org/2026/en/default.asp) in Strasbourg, France.

🌐For updates, guidelines, dataset access, and community discussions, visit the [UUSIVC2026 website](https://uusivc2026-sudo.github.io/uusivc2026.github.io/).

📄 The full challenge proposal is available [here](https://zenodo.org/records/19729665).

🔗[Baseline](https://github.com/uusivc2026-sudo/UUSIVC-2026-Challenge). It provides one possible implementation path for participating in the challenge. Participants are encouraged to explore their own approaches and develop more competitive, state-of-the-art research algorithms.

## Registration

Participants must register their team name and provide their details through a [Google Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfbO05JF__QkYzL77rdGwoFb3stit-3S5zcbVh4ALYcKjJ7AQ/viewform) before accessing the data and submitting their results. Each team has a maximum of **3 members**, including the team leader. Please ensure that you provide accurate **Codabench** usernames to enable access to data and submission permissions.

## Dataset

The UUSIVC 2026 dataset is composed of multiple public ultrasound datasets and private datasets collected in collaboration with partner hospitals.

The benchmark includes:

- B-mode ultrasound image classification.
- B-mode ultrasound image segmentation.
- CEUS video/sequence classification.
- CEUS video/frame segmentation.
- Cardiac ultrasound video/frame segmentation.

Datasets are available through two independent download sources. Please choose either one of the following links to download the dataset:

- [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/WyattH/UUSIVC2026/tree/main)
- [Baidu Netdisk](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1_8ZDKJdsR1dCsOf7XzG_ew?pwd=usvc)

Each download source contains both the training and validation data. The training set includes the input data together with the corresponding sample-level labels for classification tasks and pixel-level annotations for segmentation tasks. The validation set contains only the input data, without labels or annotations.


## Tasks

Participants are encouraged to develop a unified model or pipeline capable of handling multiple organs, modalities, and task types.
	
The online validation benchmark includes five task groups:

- **image_cls**: ultrasound image classification.
- **ceus_cls**: CEUS video/sequence classification.
- **image_seg**: 2D ultrasound image segmentation.
- **ceus_seg**: CEUS video/frame segmentation.
- **video_seg**: cardiac ultrasound video/frame segmentation.

The target organs and datasets include breast, thyroid, liver, prostate, appendix, kidney, fetal head, and cardiac structures, depending on the task type.

Representative tasks include:

- Breast lesion classification and segmentation.
- Liver disease classification.
- Appendix classification.
- Thyroid nodule segmentation.
- Kidney contour segmentation.
- Fetal head contour segmentation.
- Cardiac structure segmentation.
- Prostate image classification and segmentation.
- Cardiac video structure segmentation.
- CEUS-based classification and lesion segmentation.

Each organ is associated with a distinct clinical task, exemplifying the multi-disease and multi-task nature of the challenge. In addition to the public datasets, we will provide a small portion of our private datasets for training to mitigate domain gap difficulties. The validation and test sets will primarily consist of private data, where the validation labels and test sets will not be publicly disclosed.

## Timeline

| Phase | Dates          | Details                                                                      |
|---|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Development Phase | June 29, 2026  | Website opens for registration, release training and validation images. |
| Validation Phase | June 29, 2026  | Submission system opens for validation.                                     |
| Paper Phase | Aug. 25, 2026 | Short paper and docker submission deadline.                                  |
| Test Phase | Aug. 26, 2026 | Submission system for testing.                                         |
| Workshop | Sept. 27, 2026 | Final results are released during the Deep-Breath workshop at MICCAI 2026.    |

## Submission Guidelines

We provide guides on how to develop model, infer and submit results in the validation phase, as well as how to prepare and submit the Docker file of the model in the testing phase. Please see the **Submission Guidelines** page.

## Rules

### Methods

Participants are allowed to base their methods on existing open-source general models. And they are invited to submit a short paper (refer to Technical Report page) to the Deep-Breath workshop to introduce the details of their methods and declare innovations in areas such as preprocessing, model architecture, or post-processing.

### Use of other training data/pre-trained models
No additional data allowed;
The publicly available pre-trained model, such as ResNet50 trained on ImageNet, can be used. To ensure fairness and reproducibility of results, using unpublished pre-trained models is prohibited.

### Award Eligibility
As a condition for being ranked and considered as the challenge winner or eligible for any prize, the teams/participants must fulfil the following obligations:

- Present their method at the final event of the challenge at MICCAI 2026;
- Submit a paper to Deep-Breath workshop reporting the details of the methods in a short or long (up to the teams) LNCS format;
- Sign and return all prize acceptance documents as may be required by Competition Sponsor/Organizers;
- Commit to citing the data challenge paper and the data overview paper whenever submitting the developed method for scientific and non-scientific publications.

## Awards
Top-10 teams will be invited to present talks and winning certificates will be provided.

We will provide a prize of 9,900 CNY for the Top 10 teams.

- 1st Place: 2,500 CNY
- 2nd-3rd Place: 1,500 CNY
- 4th-6th Place: 1,200 CNY
- 7th-10th Place: 500 CNY

Sponsors for the awards are currently being investigated.

The challenge organizers aim to publish a summary paper in a relevant journal. The top ten performing teams will be invited to as co-authors. Participants can submit their own paper after submitting the summary paper or once the challenge paper is published on Arxiv.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
You can view the full FAQ on the corresponding page. And please do not hesitate to email us ([uusivc2026@gmail.com](mailto:uusivc2026@gmail.com)) if you have any questions.

# 欢迎来到UUSIVC 2026挑战赛

欢迎参加**通用超声图像与视频分析挑战赛2026：B模式和对比增强超声跨多器官分类与分割**。

本挑战赛致力于评估多器官、多模态超声图像和视频分析算法。基准测试涵盖B模式超声图像、对比增强超声(CEUS)视频和心脏超声视频的分类和分割任务。目标是推进超声图像分析中AI模型的泛化能力、鲁棒性和临床适用性。

🧪参与者将通过Codabench平台进行基准测试，利用自动化提交和评估管道，实时排行榜跟踪分类和分割任务的性能表现。

🏆挑战赛结果和获奖者将在[Deep-Breath 2026: 第3届Deep Breast工作坊——乳腺影像诊断和治疗挑战中的AI和影像学](https://deep-breath-miccai.github.io/deepbreath-2026/)期间公布，该工作坊与[MICCAI 2026](https://conferences.miccai.org/2026/en/default.asp)在法国斯特拉斯堡联合举办。

🌐如需了解最新信息、获取指南、数据集访问权限和社区讨论，请访问[UUSIVC2026网站](https://uusivc2026-sudo.github.io/uusivc2026.github.io/)。

📄完整的挑战赛方案可在[此处](https://zenodo.org/records/19729665)获取。

🔗[基准实现](https://github.com/uusivc2026-sudo/UUSIVC-2026-Challenge)。它提供了参与挑战赛的一种可能的实现路径。鼓励参与者探索自己的方法，开发更具竞争力的、最先进的研究算法。

## 注册

参与者必须通过[谷歌表单](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfbO05JF__QkYzL77rdGwoFb3stit-3S5zcbVh4ALYcKjJ7AQ/viewform)注册团队名称并提供相关信息，以获得数据访问权限并提交结果。每个团队最多包括**3名成员**，包括团队负责人。请确保提供准确的**Codabench**用户名，以启用数据访问和提交权限。

## 数据集

UUSIVC 2026数据集由多个公开超声数据集和与合作医院共同收集的私有数据集组成。

基准测试包括：

- B模式超声图像分类
- B模式超声图像分割
- CEUS视频/序列分类
- CEUS视频/帧分割
- 心脏超声视频/帧分割

数据集可通过两个独立的下载来源获取。请选择以下链接之一下载数据集：

- [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/WyattH/UUSIVC2026/tree/main)
- [百度网盘](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1_8ZDKJdsR1dCsOf7XzG_ew?pwd=usvc)

每个下载来源都包含训练和验证数据。训练集包括输入数据以及相应的样本级标签(用于分类任务)和像素级标注(用于分割任务)。验证集仅包含输入数据，不包含标签或标注。

## 任务

鼓励参与者开发能够处理多个器官、多种模态和多种任务类型的统一模型或管道。

在线验证基准包括五个任务组：

- **image_cls**：超声图像分类
- **ceus_cls**：CEUS视频/序列分类
- **image_seg**：二维超声图像分割
- **ceus_seg**：CEUS视频/帧分割
- **video_seg**：心脏超声视频/帧分割

目标器官和数据集包括乳腺、甲状腺、肝脏、前列腺、阑尾、肾脏、胎儿头部和心脏结构，具体取决于任务类型。

代表性任务包括：

- 乳腺病变分类和分割
- 肝病分类
- 阑尾分类
- 甲状腺结节分割
- 肾脏轮廓分割

# Submission Guidelines

This page describes the required submission format for the validation and testing phases.

**Important: Participants should register their team name and participants via a [Google Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfbO05JF__QkYzL77rdGwoFb3stit-3S5zcbVh4ALYcKjJ7AQ/viewform) before participating.**

## Development Phase

To help participants quickly get familiar with the data processing and model building workflow, we provide the training code and pre-trained weights for our baseline model [here](https://github.com/uusivc2026-sudo/UUSIVC-2026-Challenge). Participants are encouraged to use this baseline as a starting point to build and customize their own approach, or alternatively, develop a completely new method from scratch based on their own ideas.

## Submission type

The validation phase uses **result submission**.

Participants should submit prediction files. The submitted archive should contain:

```text
classification.json
image_seg/<Dataset>/masks/*.png
ceus_seg/<Dataset>/annotations/*.npz
video_seg/<Dataset>/annotations/*.npz
```

The top level of the zip file must directly contain `classification.json`, `image_seg`, `ceus_seg`, and `video_seg`. Do not wrap them inside an extra parent folder.

Correct:

```text
submission.zip
-- classification.json
-- image_seg/
-- ceus_seg/
-- video_seg/
```

Incorrect:

```text
submission.zip
-- my_submission_folder/
    -- classification.json
    -- image_seg/
    -- ceus_seg/
    -- video_seg/
```

## Classification prediction format

Task4 ImageCls includes Appendix, Breast, Liver, and Prostate. Task5 CEUSCls includes BreastCEUS, LiverCEUS, ProstateCEUS, and ThyroidCEUS.


Classification predictions should be saved in a JSON file named:

```text
classification.json
```

The JSON should map either `sample_id` or `input_path_relative` to a prediction object. We recommend using `input_path_relative` because it is easy to match with `datalist.json`.

Example:

```json
{
  "ceus_cls/Breast/videos/cls_00000.npy": {
    "prediction": 1,
    "probability": [0.2, 0.8]
  },
  "image_cls/Appendix/imgs/cls_00000.jpg": {
    "prediction": 0,
    "probability": [0.9, 0.1]
  }
}
```

Fields:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `prediction` | Predicted class index. |
| `probability` | Class probability list. |

For binary classification tasks, `probability` should contain two values:

## Image segmentation prediction format

Task1 ImageSeg includes Breast, Fetal Head, Heart, Kidney, Thyroid, and Prostate.


For `image_seg`, predictions should be grayscale mask images.

Required folder structure:

```text
image_seg/<Dataset>/masks/<mask_name>.png
```

Example:

```text
image_seg/Breast/masks/seg_mask_00000.png
image_seg/Thyroid/masks/seg_mask_00000.png
image_seg/Prostate/masks/seg_mask_00000.png
```

Mask requirements:

- Single-channel grayscale PNG is recommended.
- Background should be `0`.
- Foreground can be any non-zero value, preferably `255`.
- If the submitted mask size differs from the reference size, the scorer will resize the prediction to the reference size using nearest-neighbor interpolation.

## CEUS segmentation prediction format

For `ceus_seg`, predictions should be saved as `.npz` files under:

```text
ceus_seg/<Dataset>/annotations/<annotation_name>.npz
```

Example:

```text
ceus_seg/BreastCEUS/annotations/seg_annotation_00000.npz
ceus_seg/LiverCEUS/annotations/seg_annotation_00000.npz
```

The expected `.npz` file should contain a key named `mask`:

```python
import numpy as np

mask = np.zeros((256, 512), dtype=np.uint8)
# mask[predicted_foreground > 0] = 255
np.savez("seg_annotation_00000.npz", mask=mask)
```

Mask requirements:

- `mask` should be a 2D array.
- Background should be `0`.
- Foreground can be any non-zero value, preferably `255`.

## Video segmentation prediction format

For `video_seg`, predictions should be saved as `.npz` files under:

```text
video_seg/<Dataset>/annotations/<annotation_name>.npz
```

Example:

```text
video_seg/CardiacCH/annotations/seg_annotation_00000.npz
```

The expected `.npz` file should contain a dictionary named `fnum_mask`, where each key is a frame index and each value is a 2D mask array.

Example:

```python
import numpy as np

fnum_mask = {
    "0": np.zeros((256, 256), dtype=np.uint8),
    "14": np.zeros((256, 256), dtype=np.uint8),
    "33": np.zeros((256, 256), dtype=np.uint8),
}

np.savez("seg_annotation_00000.npz", fnum_mask=fnum_mask)
```

Mask requirements:

- Keys should match the annotated frame indices provided in `datalist.json`.
- Each mask should be a 2D array.
- Background should be `0`.
- Foreground can be any non-zero value, preferably `255`.

## Submission archive checklist

Before uploading, check that the zip file directly contains the required prediction files and folders:

```text
submission.zip
-- classification.json
-- image_seg/
-- ceus_seg/
-- video_seg/
```

## Validation scoring

The online validation ranking is based on evaluation metrics only.

For classification datasets:

```text
classification dataset score = 0.5 * Accuracy + 0.5 * AUC
```

For segmentation samples or annotated frames:

```text
case/frame segmentation score = 0.7 * DSC + 0.3 * NSD
```

Dataset-level and task-family scores are aggregated using dataset-size-based weights.

The online validation score is:

```text
overall_score = mean(Task1, Task2, Task3, Task4, Task5)
```

Efficiency metrics such as runtime and GPU memory are not included in the online validation ranking.

## Testing Phase

### Submission Requirements
During the testing phase, each team must submit:
- A Docker image containing your method
    - This image will be used by the organizers to run and evaluate your model.
    - Please follow the Docker building instructions.
- A 4-page technical report in Word or PDF format, which must include:
  - Team Name
  - Team Leader’s Name
  - Team Members
  - Affiliation
  - The content should describe your approach, methodology, and any important implementation details.

### Submission Method
Please send both files by email to the organizing committee:

- Email Address: [uusivc2026@gmail.com](uusivc2026@gmail.com)
- Subject Format: UUSIC-Testing Phase Submission-[TeamName]
- Attachments:
  - Docker image file (or a link to download it) or Docker Hub link
  - Technical report (Word or PDF)

## Important Notes
Only teams that submit both the Docker image and the technical report will be eligible to:

- Participate in the testing phase
- Appear in the final ranking
- Receive prize awards
- Be included as co-authors in the post-challenge paper
- Submissions that do not follow the Docker build instructions may fail to run during evaluation.

# Scoring Formulas

The algorithm will be assessed using the following metrics, and all metrics will be used to compute the ranking. The implementation of the used metrics can be found [here](https://github.com/uusic2025/challenge/blob/main/evaluation/metrics.py)

## Segmentation Metrics

### Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)

Dice Similarity Coefficient measures the overlap between the predicted segmentation mask and the ground-truth segmentation mask.

### Normalized Surface Dice (NSD)

Normalized Surface Dice evaluates boundary agreement between the predicted mask and the ground-truth mask within a tolerance distance.


## Classification Metrics

### Area Under Curve (AUC)

Area Under Curve evaluates classification performance across decision thresholds.

### Accuracy

Accuracy measures the proportion of correctly classified samples.


## Task-wise Scores

The validation leaderboard is organized into five task groups:

- **Task1 ImageSeg**: B-mode ultrasound image segmentation, including Breast, Fetal Head, Heart, Kidney, Thyroid, and Prostate.
- **Task2 CEUSSeg**: CEUS lesion segmentation, including BreastCEUS, LiverCEUS, ProstateCEUS, and ThyroidCEUS.
- **Task3 VideoSeg**: cardiac ultrasound video/frame segmentation, including CardiacCH.
- **Task4 ImageCls**: B-mode ultrasound image classification, including Appendix, Breast, Liver, and Prostate.
- **Task5 CEUSCls**: CEUS video/sequence classification, including BreastCEUS, LiverCEUS, ProstateCEUS, and ThyroidCEUS.

For each classification dataset:

```text
dataset score = 0.5 * Accuracy + 0.5 * AUC
```

For each segmentation sample or annotated frame:

```text
case/frame score = 0.7 * DSC + 0.3 * NSD
```

Each task score is the sample-weighted average of its datasets. The online validation ranking score is the equal-weighted average of the five task scores:

```text
overall_score = mean(Task1, Task2, Task3, Task4, Task5)
```

## Online Validation Ranking

The online validation leaderboard is ranked by performance metrics only. Efficiency terms such as running time and GPU memory are not included in the Codabench validation score because validation submissions are prediction files and are not executed in a unified hardware environment.

For the final test stage, selected teams will submit Docker containers. The organizers will run the containers offline on unified hardware and may report computational efficiency separately.

# 评分公式

该算法将使用以下指标进行评估，所有指标都将用于计算排名。使用指标的实现可以在[这里](https://github.com/uusic2025/challenge/blob/main/evaluation/metrics.py)找到。

## 分割指标

### Dice 相似系数 (DSC)

Dice 相似系数衡量预测分割掩膜与真实值分割掩膜之间的重叠程度。

### 归一化表面 Dice (NSD)

归一化表面 Dice 评估预测掩膜与真实值掩膜在容差距离内的边界一致性。


## 分类指标

### 曲线下面积 (AUC)

曲线下面积评估分类模型在不同决策阈值下的性能。

### 准确度

准确度衡量正确分类样本的比例。


## 任务级评分

验证排行榜分为五个任务组：

- **任务1 ImageSeg**：B模式超声图像分割，包括乳腺、胎儿头部、心脏、肾脏、甲状腺和前列腺。
- **任务2 CEUSSeg**：造影超声病灶分割，包括乳腺造影超声、肝脏造影超声、前列腺造影超声和甲状腺造影超声。
- **任务3 VideoSeg**：心脏超声视频/帧分割，包括心脏造影超声。
- **任务4 ImageCls**：B模式超声图像分类，包括阑尾、乳腺、肝脏和前列腺。
- **任务5 CEUSCls**：造影超声视频/序列分类，包括乳腺造影超声、肝脏造影超声、前列腺造影超声和甲状腺造影超声。

对于每个分类数据集：

```text
数据集评分 = 0.5 × 准确度 + 0.5 × AUC
```

对于每个分割样本或标注帧：

```text
样本/帧评分 = 0.7 × DSC + 0.3 × NSD
```

每个任务评分是其数据集的样本加权平均值。在线验证排名评分是五个任务评分的等权平均值：

```text
总体评分 = 平均值(任务1, 任务2, 任务3, 任务4, 任务5)
```

## 在线验证排名

在线验证排行榜仅按性能指标排名。由于验证提交是预测文件，不在统一硬件环境中执行，因此评分中不包含运行时间和GPU显存等效率指标。

对于最终测试阶段，入选团队需提交Docker容器。组织者将在统一硬件上离线运行这些容器，并可能单独报告计算效率。

17555.title: 2026 “金睛杯”光学时敏弱小目标探测挑战赛（赛道一：红外视频卫星空中动目标检测）
17555.description:
光学时敏弱小目标探测是智能视觉感知领域中的重要研究方向，也是复杂环境下目标探测与态势感知中的关键技术问题。与常规目标检测任务相比，弱小目标通常存在成像尺度小、目标能量弱、背景干扰强、目标形态不稳定等特点，单帧图像中可利用的信息十分有限，算法在真实场景中容易出现漏检、误检和检测结果不连续等问题。
本次挑战赛依托 CSIG2026 学术会议平台，围绕光学时敏弱小目标探测中的关键问题，设置"红外视频卫星空中动目标检测"和"基于事件相机的运动小目标检测"两个赛道，为参赛队伍提供公平、可复现的算法验证平台，推动相关数据建设、方法创新和技术交流。
17555.description_zh:
Optical temporal-sensitive small target detection is an important research direction in intelligent visual perception and a key technical issue in target detection and situational awareness in complex environments. Compared with conventional target detection tasks, small targets typically exhibit characteristics such as small imaging scale, weak target energy, strong background interference, and unstable target morphology. The information available in a single frame is very limited, and algorithms are prone to missed detections, false positives, and discontinuous detection results in real-world scenarios.

This challenge competition, based on the CSIG2026 academic conference platform, focuses on key problems in optical temporal-sensitive small target detection, establishing two tracks: "infrared video satellite aerial moving target detection" and "event camera-based moving small target detection." It provides participating teams with a fair and reproducible algorithm validation platform, promoting related data construction, method innovation, and technical exchange.

pages.title: 赛事说明
pages.content:
## 挑战赛的目的 **通过本次挑战赛促进科研技术的交流研讨和应用推广** 本次挑战赛旨在依托 CSIG2026 学术会议平台，围绕光学时敏弱小目标探测中的关键问题，搭建面向学术界和产业界的开放竞赛与交流平台，吸引更多高校、科研院所和企业团队参与红外视频小目标检测、事件相机小目标检测等方向的研究。 **通过本次挑战赛促进光学时敏弱小目标探测技术发展** 通过竞赛汇聚工业界和学术界的智慧与力量，促进相关算法、数据集和评价体系的共同发展，推动领域垂类大模型发展与应用，加速技术创新和产业推广。 --- ## 挑战赛的意义 **光学时敏弱小目标探测应用广泛，关键技术问题突出** 光学时敏弱小目标探测是智能视觉感知领域中的重要研究方向，也是复杂环境下目标探测与态势感知中的关键技术问题。弱小目标通常存在成像尺度小、目标能量弱、背景干扰强、目标形态不稳定等特点，单帧图像中可利用的信息十分有限。 **红外视频卫星目标检测亟需融合时域信息与轨迹关联** 卫星视角下的红外视频弱小目标往往具有成像距离远、信噪比低、背景复杂、运动轨迹细弱等特点，仅依靠单帧检测难以获得稳定结果，需要进一步结合多帧时域信息、运动一致性和目标轨迹关联关系。 **事件相机小目标检测亟需发挥事件流时空连续性优势** 事件相机能够以异步方式感知亮度变化，具有高时间分辨率、低延迟、高动态范围和低数据冗余等优势。面向事件点云和事件流的时空建模方法发展，对于提升复杂场景下运动小目标的检测能力具有重要意义。 **公开数据和统一评测标准有助于推动领域发展** 红外视频卫星目标和事件相机小目标相关公开数据仍相对有限，真实场景数据获取和标注成本较高。本次竞赛通过开放具有针对性的数据资源和统一评测标准，为参赛队伍提供公平、可复现的算法验证平台。 --- ## 任务设置 ### 赛道一：红外视频卫星空中动目标检测 赛道一的主要任务是对视频中的红外小目标的质心进行预测，附加任务是对目标进行跟踪。参赛队伍根据红外小目标图像特点自行设计相关算法，使用主办方提供的数据集进行模型训练，最终以召回率（Recall）、精确率（Precision）和 F1 分数作为评价指标，以及轨迹完整度和轨迹准确度作为附加评价指标，衡量参赛队伍算法模型的性能。 ### 赛道二：基于事件相机的运动小目标检测 赛道二的主要任务是对事件流中的目标事件进行逐事件分割。参赛队伍根据事件小目标特性自行设计相关算法，使用主办方提供的事件数据集进行模型训练，最终以交并比（IoU）、准确率（ACC）、检测率（Pd）和虚警率（Fa）作为主要评价指标，衡量参赛队伍算法模型的性能。 --- ## 数据集简介 ### 赛道一数据集简介 竞赛数据集由国防科技大学与武汉大学联合开发，包括：基于热红外卫星的 IRAir 数据集、基于 Landsat 卫星的 IRSatVideo-LEO 数据集、基于高分四号卫星的 IRSatVideo-GEO 数据集，以及实测卫星热红外视频数据，共 1400 段视频序列（1000 段用于训练，200 段用于验证，200 段用于测试）。比赛开始前，将发布训练集和验证集视频及掩码标注；进入评测阶段时公布测试集视频，测试集标签不公开。 | 数据集 | 数据集简介 | 图像与目标示意 | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | IRAir | 数据来源：热红外 SDG 卫星一号图像，仿真目标
目标特点：飞机，低轨，暗目标
分辨率：256×256 | | | IRSatVideo-LEO | 数据来源：Landsat 卫星图像，仿真目标
目标特点：低轨，亮目标，短波红外
分辨率：1024×1024 | | | IRSatVideo-GEO | 数据来源：高分四号卫星图像，仿真目标
目标特点：地球同步轨道，中波红外，弱目标
分辨率：742×733（平均） | | | 实测热红外视频数据 | 数据来源：实测卫星热红外视频
目标特点：长波
分辨率：512×640 | | ### 赛道二数据集简介 基于 DAVIS346 事件相机的 EV-UAV 数据集作为训练、验证和测试数据集。总共 147 段序列（99 段用于训练，24 段用于验证，24 段用于测试）。（暂定） | 数据集 | 数据集简介 | 图像与目标示意 | | :---: | :---: | :---:| | EV-UAV  | 数据来源：DAVIS346 事件相机实拍
分辨率：346×260 | | --- ## 挑战赛评价方式 ### 赛道一评价方式 本次挑战赛赛道一的算法评价指标为召回率（Recall）和精确率（Precision），附加评价指标为轨迹完整度、轨迹准确度。算法最终评分结果由 F1 分数和附加分数组成。 $$ Recall = \frac{TD}{AT}, \quad Precision = \frac{TD}{TD + FD} $$ $$ F1 = \frac{2 \times Recall \times Precision}{Recall + Precision} $$ $$ TrackCompleteness = \frac{NTA}{N}, \quad TrackAccuracy = \frac{NTA}{NA} $$ | 附加得分项 | 阈值一 | 阈值二 | 阈值三 | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | 轨迹完整度得分 | ≥25%：+2分 | ≥35%：+3分 | ≥50%：+5分 | | 轨迹准确度得分 | ≥55%：+2分 | ≥65%：+3分 | ≥80%：+5分 | 最终得分为 F1 分数 × 100 + 附加得分，满分为 110 分。 --- ### 赛道二评价方式 赛道二的算法评价指标为交并比（IoU）、准确率（Acc）、检测率（Pd）和虚警率（Fa），最终评分结果由各指标加权得分。 $$ IoU = \frac{GT \cap Pred}{GT \cup Pred}, \quad Acc = \frac{TP_{target}}{TP_{target} + FN_{target}} $$ $$ Pd = \frac{TD}{AT}, \quad Fa = \frac{FD}{N_{frame} \times H \times W} $$ $$ Score_{Fa} = e^{-10000 \times Fa} $$ $$ Score = 0.4Pd + 0.3Score_{Fa} + 0.2IoU + 0.1Acc $$ --- ## 结果提交方式 **结果提交格式、提交入口和提交次数限制**：待补充 **提交内容与时间要求**：参赛队伍须在规定时间内提交测试结果，并在后继阶段提交算法代码、模型文件及算法报告。组委会将对各参赛队伍进行真实性审查。 **真实性与可复现性要求**：为避免参赛队伍滥用其他数据集或验证集标签信息用于算法训练，参赛队伍需提供算法训练时的相关参数，确保算法结果可复现。如发现违规使用数据信息或算法结果无法复现，组委会将按赛事规则处理。 --- ## 专题研讨会 组委会将举办挑战赛技术论坛，邀请获得一、二等奖的参赛队伍参加作特邀技术报告。 --- ## 知识产权归属 参赛队伍提交的算法及可执行模型的知识产权归参赛团队所有，比赛数据集归主办方所有。 各参赛队伍需要承诺提交的结果可重复，组织方承诺履行保密义务，并不用于除本挑战赛外的任何其他用途。 参赛队伍应保证所提供的方案、算法属于自有知识产权。组织方对参赛队伍因使用本队提供完成的算法和结果而产生的任何实际侵权或者被任何第三方指控侵权概不负责。一旦上述情况和事件发生，参赛队伍必须承担一切相关法律责任和经济赔偿责任并保护组织方免于承担该等责任。

17556.description:
光学时敏弱小目标探测是智能视觉感知领域中的重要研究方向，也是复杂环境下目标探测与态势感知中的关键技术问题。与常规目标检测任务相比，弱小目标通常存在成像尺度小、目标能量弱、背景干扰强、目标形态不稳定等特点，单帧图像中可利用的信息十分有限，算法在真实场景中容易出现漏检、误检和检测结果不连续等问题。
本次挑战赛依托 CSIG2026 学术会议平台，围绕光学时敏弱小目标探测中的关键问题，设置"红外视频卫星空中动目标检测"和"基于事件相机的运动小目标检测"两个赛道，为参赛队伍提供公平、可复现的算法验证平台，推动相关数据建设、方法创新和技术交流。
17556.description_zh:
Optical Time-Sensitive Weak-Small Target Detection is an important research direction in intelligent visual perception and a key technical challenge in target detection and situation awareness in complex environments. Compared to conventional target detection tasks, weak-small targets typically exhibit characteristics such as small imaging scale, weak target energy, strong background interference, and unstable target morphology. The usable information in a single frame image is extremely limited, and algorithms are prone to issues such as missed detections, false detections, and discontinuous detection results in real-world scenarios.

This challenge competition, based on the CSIG2026 academic conference platform, focuses on key problems in optical time-sensitive weak-small target detection, and sets up two competition tracks: "Infrared Video Satellite Airborne Moving Target Detection" and "Motion Small Target Detection Based on Event Camera". It provides participating teams with a fair and reproducible algorithm validation platform, promoting advances in related data construction, method innovation, and technical exchange.

## 挑战赛的目的 **通过本次挑战赛促进科研技术的交流研讨和应用推广** 本次挑战赛旨在依托 CSIG2026 学术会议平台，围绕光学时敏弱小目标探测中的关键问题，搭建面向学术界和产业界的开放竞赛与交流平台，吸引更多高校、科研院所和企业团队参与红外视频小目标检测、事件相机小目标检测等方向的研究。 **通过本次挑战赛促进光学时敏弱小目标探测技术发展** 通过竞赛汇聚工业界和学术界的智慧与力量，促进相关算法、数据集和评价体系的共同发展，推动领域垂类大模型发展与应用，加速技术创新和产业推广。 --- ## 挑战赛的意义 **光学时敏弱小目标探测应用广泛，关键技术问题突出** 光学时敏弱小目标探测是智能视觉感知领域中的重要研究方向，也是复杂环境下目标探测与态势感知中的关键技术问题。弱小目标通常存在成像尺度小、目标能量弱、背景干扰强、目标形态不稳定等特点，单帧图像中可利用的信息十分有限。 **红外视频卫星目标检测亟需融合时域信息与轨迹关联** 卫星视角下的红外视频弱小目标往往具有成像距离远、信噪比低、背景复杂、运动轨迹细弱等特点，仅依靠单帧检测难以获得稳定结果，需要进一步结合多帧时域信息、运动一致性和目标轨迹关联关系。 **事件相机小目标检测亟需发挥事件流时空连续性优势** 事件相机能够以异步方式感知亮度变化，具有高时间分辨率、低延迟、高动态范围和低数据冗余等优势。面向事件点云和事件流的时空建模方法发展，对于提升复杂场景下运动小目标的检测能力具有重要意义。 **公开数据和统一评测标准有助于推动领域发展** 红外视频卫星目标和事件相机小目标相关公开数据仍相对有限，真实场景数据获取和标注成本较高。本次竞赛通过开放具有针对性的数据资源和统一评测标准，为参赛队伍提供公平、可复现的算法验证平台。 --- ## 任务设置 ### 赛道一：红外视频卫星空中动目标检测 赛道一的主要任务是对视频中的红外小目标的质心进行预测，附加任务是对目标进行跟踪。参赛队伍根据红外小目标图像特点自行设计相关算法，使用主办方提供的数据集进行模型训练，最终以召回率（Recall）、精确率（Precision）和 F1 分数作为评价指标，以及轨迹完整度和轨迹准确度作为附加评价指标，衡量参赛队伍算法模型的性能。 ### 赛道二：基于事件相机的运动小目标检测 赛道二的主要任务是对事件流中的目标事件进行逐事件分割。参赛队伍根据事件小目标特性自行设计相关算法，使用主办方提供的事件数据集进行模型训练，最终以交并比（IoU）、准确率（ACC）、检测率（Pd）和虚警率（Fa）作为主要评价指标，衡量参赛队伍算法模型的性能。 --- ## 数据集简介 ### 赛道一数据集简介 竞赛数据集由国防科技大学与武汉大学联合开发，包括：基于热红外卫星的 IRAir 数据集、基于 Landsat 卫星的 IRSatVideo-LEO 数据集、基于高分四号卫星的 IRSatVideo-GEO 数据集，以及实测卫星热红外视频数据，共 1400 段视频序列（1000 段用于训练，200 段用于验证，200 段用于测试）。比赛开始前，将发布训练集和验证集视频及掩码标注；进入评测阶段时公布测试集视频，测试集标签不公开。 | 数据集 | 数据集简介 | 图像与目标示意 | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | IRAir | 数据来源：热红外 SDG 卫星一号图像，仿真目标
目标特点：飞机，低轨，暗目标
分辨率：256×256 | | | IRSatVideo-LEO | 数据来源：Landsat 卫星图像，仿真目标
目标特点：低轨，亮目标，短波红外
分辨率：1024×1024 | | | IRSatVideo-GEO | 数据来源：高分四号卫星图像，仿真目标
目标特点：地球同步轨道，中波红外，弱目标
分辨率：742×733（平均） | | | 实测热红外视频数据 | 数据来源：实测卫星热红外视频
目标特点：长波
分辨率：512×640 | | ### 赛道二数据集简介 基于 DAVIS346 事件相机的 EV-UAV 数据集作为训练、验证和测试数据集。总共 147 段序列（99 段用于训练，24 段用于验证，24 段用于测试）。（暂定） | 数据集 | 数据集简介 | 图像与目标示意 | | :---: | :---: | :---:| | EV-UAV  | 数据来源：DAVIS346 事件相机实拍
分辨率：346×260 | | --- ## 挑战赛评价方式 ### 赛道一评价方式 本次挑战赛赛道一的算法评价指标为召回率（Recall）和精确率（Precision），附加评价指标为轨迹完整度、轨迹准确度。算法最终评分结果由 F1 分数和附加分数组成。 $$ Recall = \frac{TD}{AT}, \quad Precision = \frac{TD}{TD + FD} $$ $$ F1 = \frac{2 \times Recall \times Precision}{Recall + Precision} $$ $$ TrackCompleteness = \frac{NTA}{N}, \quad TrackAccuracy = \frac{NTA}{NA} $$ | 附加得分项 | 阈值一 | 阈值二 | 阈值三 | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | 轨迹完整度得分 | ≥25%：+2分 | ≥35%：+3分 | ≥50%：+5分 | | 轨迹准确度得分 | ≥55%：+2分 | ≥65%：+3分 | ≥80%：+5分 | 最终得分为 F1 分数 × 100 + 附加得分，满分为 110 分。 --- ### 赛道二评价方式 赛道二的算法评价指标为交并比（IoU）、准确率（Acc）、检测率（Pd）和虚警率（Fa），最终评分结果由各指标加权得分。 $$ IoU = \frac{GT \cap Pred}{GT \cup Pred}, \quad Acc = \frac{TP_{target}}{TP_{target} + FN_{target}} $$ $$ Pd = \frac{TD}{AT}, \quad Fa = \frac{FD}{N_{frame} \times H \times W} $$ $$ Score_{Fa} = e^{-10000 \times Fa} $$ $$ Score = 0.4Pd + 0.3Score_{Fa} + 0.2IoU + 0.1Acc $$ --- ## 结果提交方式 **结果提交格式、提交入口和提交次数限制**：待补充 **提交内容与时间要求**：参赛队伍须在规定时间内提交测试结果，并在后继阶段提交算法代码、模型文件及算法报告。组委会将对各参赛队伍进行真实性审查。 **真实性与可复现性要求**：为避免参赛队伍滥用其他数据集或验证集标签信息用于算法训练，参赛队伍需提供算法训练时的相关参数，确保算法结果可复现。如发现违规使用数据信息或算法结果无法复现，组委会将按赛事规则处理。 --- ## 专题研讨会 组委会将举办挑战赛技术论坛，邀请获得一、二等奖的参赛队伍参加作特邀技术报告。 --- ## 知识产权归属 参赛队伍提交的算法及可执行模型的知识产权归参赛团队所有，比赛数据集归主办方所有。 各参赛队伍需要承诺提交的结果可重复，组织方承诺履行保密义务，并不用于除本挑战赛外的任何其他用途。 参赛队伍应保证所提供的方案、算法属于自有知识产权。组织方对参赛队伍因使用本队提供完成的算法和结果而产生的任何实际侵权或者被任何第三方指控侵权概不负责。一旦上述情况和事件发生，参赛队伍必须承担一切相关法律责任和经济赔偿责任并保护组织方免于承担该等责任。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
##
[MICCAI FLARE26](https://flare-medfm.github.io/) Task 2: AutoMSC: Automated Medical image Segmentation and Classification
Deep learning models for 3D medical imaging have traditionally been handcrafted for individual tasks, either segmentation or classification, requiring extensive manual tuning of architectures, hyperparameters, and preprocessing pipelines. As clinical datasets grow in scale and complexity, this manual design process becomes increasingly inefficient and limits the deployment of adaptable, general-purpose models. Motivated by the success of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon challenge and nnU-Net (the winning solution), Task 2 focuses on building self-configured models capable of automatically adapting to diverse 3D medical imaging datasets while simultaneously performing both segmentation and classification. This task aims to advance the next generation of autonomous modeldesign systems for 3D medical imaging. Participants are required to design models that can automatically infer optimal configurations (e.g., architecture, resolution, patch size, normalization strategy, and loss balancing) and jointly learn highquality segmentation masks and clinically meaningful classification labels. These models should generalize across imaging modality, tumor types without taskspecific manual engineering, including prostate cancer recurrence prediction in MRI scans, lung nodule diagnosis in CT scans, and liver metastasis origin prediction in PET/CT scans. Key Features: - **Multi-task Learning**: Models must perform both 3D segmentation and classification from the same input volume, optimizing for accuracy in both outputs while maintaining computational efficiency. - **Self-configuration**: Solutions should include automated configuration mechanisms capable of adapting to dataset properties, such as voxel spacing, image size, contrast variability, and class imbalance, without human-designed heuristics. - **Dataset Diversity**: The benchmark includes heterogeneous 3D medical imaging scans with varying modalities (CT, MRI, and PET-CT) and classification targets, encouraging the development of truly generalizable 3D models. - **Robustness and Efficiency**: Models will be evaluated on segmentation accuracy (DSC and NSD), classification performance (balanced accuracy and AUROC), and resource efficiency (runtime), highlighting their potential for real-world clinical adoption. Participants are also encouraged to explore other challenge tracks at https://flare-medfm.github.io/, including: pan-cancer segmentation, and multimodal models. --- ## 🚀 Join the challenge (2026.04.01-8.30) * Register an account on this website and join the challenge * Fill out the [registration form](https://forms.gle/my1MimQ758oDyhWb9) Note: To change team information, please simply re-submit the form. * Test your account by making a submission with [baseline](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Awx9GE4kMNBCdZa0nxc5957f327tlQb5/view?usp=drive_link) * Request Dataset [FLARE-AutoMSC](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FLARE-MedFM/FLARE-AutoMSC). We will approve your request in 1-2 working days after reviewing your application. Remarks: * This challenge has two tracks: 1) Unified models for joint segmentation and classification (e.g., [JSC](https://github.com/bowang-lab/JSC)). 2) Independent models for segmentation (e.g., [nnUNet](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet)) or classification ([nnClass](https://github.com/bowang-lab/nnClass)). Participants can join one track or both tracks. * For both tracks, solutions should include automated configuration mechanisms capable of adapting to different datasets. * Clinical data (if available) is optional but encouraged for model development. * If you have any questions that are not listed on the QA page, please reach out to chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com --- ## 🏊‍ Validation submission (2026.4.20-8.30) * All teams can directly submit the validation results on the challenge page to get the metrics. * To get the runtime metrics, participants are allowed to make one docker submission every week by sending email to chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com. ### Baseline Docker output([example](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FA1eVlaJuXy9uOtpZY-2AXnQqNQLQGLc/view?usp=drive_link)) ### Submission format ([example](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Awx9GE4kMNBCdZa0nxc5957f327tlQb5/view?usp=drive_link)) Submit a **single ZIP** whose contents sit in one **flat** directory (no sub-folders): ``` submission.zip ├── predictions.csv # classification predictions ├── BT0001.nii.gz # predicted segmentation masks (same level as the CSV) ├── BT0007.nii.gz └── ... ``` **Segmentation masks** — one file per case, named `{identifier}.nii.gz` (e.g. `BT0001.nii.gz`), binary whole-tumor label (`1` = tumor, `0` = background), same geometry (spacing orientation, and origin) as the input image. **predictions.csv** — one row per case, with the exact column headers (case-sensitive, in this order): | Column | Description | |--------|---------| | `identifier` | case ID, e.g. `BT0001` | | `idh_wildtype` | Probability(IDH = Unaltered / wild-type) | | `idh_mutated` | Probability(IDH = Altered / mutated) | | `grade2` | Probability(Grade 2) | |`grade3` | Probability(Grade 3) | | `grade4` | Probability(Grade 4) | Example: |identifier|idh_wildtype|idh_mutated|grade2|grade3|grade4| |--------|---------|--------|---------|--------|---------| |BT0001|0.90|0.10|0.10|0.30|0.60| |BT0007|0.15|0.85|0.05|0.25|0.70| Notes: * Column headers and mask filenames must match exactly so predictions can be paired with the ground truth; missing cases are scored 0. * Model ensemble are not allowed in this competition. (If the data contains two different classification tasks, it's allowed to train two separate models but it's not allowed to train multiple models (or multi-fold ensemble) for ensemble for the same classification task.) --- ## 🏹 Testing submission (2026.9.1-9.7) The submitted Docker container will be evaluated with the following commands. If the Docker container does not work or the paper does not include all the necessary information to reproduce the method, we will return back the error information and review comments to participants. docker load -i teamname.tar.gz docker container run --gpus "device=1" -m 28G --name teamname --rm -v \$PWD/FLARE_Test/:/workspace/inputs/ -v \$PWD/teamname_outputs/:/workspace/outputs/ teamname:latest /bin/bash -c "sh predict.sh" ## Paper submission(Due on 9.14) Please parepare the paper with this [template-tbd]() and submit it on [openreview](https://openreview.net/group) by Sep. 14, 2026. Please carefully read the template and the common issue before writing the manuscript. The evaluation process mainly focuses on the paper's completeness. Don't worry about the low performance. Since this task is very challenging, all attempts are worth sharing with readers. We will not reject papers because of Iow performance. --- ## 🏆 Awards - If there are more than 20 testing docker submissions, we will provide cash prizes for the top 5 teams (Amazon gift cards with 300/200/150/100/100 CAD, respectively) and souvenirs for the top 6-10 teams. Otherwise, only the winning team will be provided with the cash prize. - The top 5 teams will be invited to give oral presentations during MICCAI 2026. - The first author of the top 5 teams will be invited to contribute to a challenge summary paper. - A certificate will be awarded to the top 10 teams. (Top teams should make their code publicly available on GitHub for reproducibility.) - All teams have the opportunity to publish their methods in the challenge proceeding (Tentative LNCS, EI Index). [Here](https://link.springer.com/conference/flare) is an example of our previous FLARE Challenge. The challenge summary paper will be submitted to top-tired journals. Here are some of our previous summaries: * "Fast and low-GPU-memory abdomen CT organ segmentation: the flare challenge." Medical Image Analysis 82 (2022): 102616. * "Unleashing the strengths of unlabeled data in pan-cancer abdominal organ quantification: the flare22 challenge." Lancet Digital Health (2024). * "The multimodality cell segmentation challenge: toward universal solutions." Nature Methods (2024): 21, 1103–1113.

## <center>[MICCAI FLARE26](https://flare-medfm.github.io/) 任务2: AutoMSC: 自动医学图像分割和分类</center>

用于3D医学成像的深度学习模型传统上是为单个任务(分割或分类)手工设计的，需要对架构、超参数和预处理管道进行大量手动调整。随着临床数据集规模和复杂性的增加，这种手动设计过程变得越来越低效，限制了自适应通用模型的部署。受医学分割十项全能挑战赛和获胜方案nnU-Net成功的启发，任务2侧重于构建能够自动适应多样化3D医学成像数据集，同时执行分割和分类的自配置模型。

本任务旨在推进3D医学成像自主模型设计系统的下一代发展。参赛者需要设计能够自动推断最优配置(如架构、分辨率、补丁大小、归一化策略和损失平衡)的模型，并联合学习高质量分割掩码和临床有意义的分类标签。这些模型应能跨成像模态、肿瘤类型进行泛化，无需特定任务的手动工程，包括MRI扫描中的前列腺癌复发预测、CT扫描中的肺结节诊断和PET/CT扫描中的肝转移灶来源预测。

主要特征：

- **多任务学习**：模型必须从同一输入体积执行3D分割和分类，同时优化两个输出的精度并保持计算效率。
- **自配置**：解决方案应包含自动配置机制，能够适应数据集属性，如体素间距、图像大小、对比度变异性和类不平衡，无需人工设计的启发式方法。
- **数据集多样性**：基准包括具有不同模态(CT、MRI和PET-CT)和分类目标的异构3D医学成像扫描，促进真正可泛化3D模型的开发。
- **鲁棒性和效率**：模型将基于分割精度(DSC和NSD)、分类性能(平衡精度和AUROC)和资源效率(运行时间)进行评估，突出其在实际临床应用中的潜力。

参赛者还被鼓励探索其他挑战赛道，网址为https://flare-medfm.github.io/，包括：泛癌症分割和多模态模型。

---

## 🚀 加入挑战赛(2026.04.01开放)

* 在本网站注册账户并加入挑战赛
* 填写[注册表](https://forms.gle/my1MimQ758oDyhWb9)   注：若需修改团队信息，请重新提交表格。
* 申请数据集[FLARE-AutoMSC](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FLARE-MedFM/FLARE-AutoMSC)。我们将在审核申请后1-2个工作日内批准您的申请。

备注：
* 本挑战赛分为两个赛道：1) 用于联合分割和分类的统一模型(如[JSC](https://github.com/bowang-lab/JSC))。2) 用于分割(如[nnUNet](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet))或分类的独立模型([nnClass](https://github.com/bowang-lab/nnClass))。参赛者可参加一个或两个赛道。
* 对于两个赛道，解决方案应包含能够适应不同数据集的自动配置机制。
* 如有常见问题页面未列出的问题，请联系chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com

---

## Datasets

### Dataset 001 — BrainMets (PROTEAS)
* A longitudinal multi-modal brain metastasis dataset with 6 co-registered channels (T1, T1c, T2, FLAIR, CT, RTP). Provides **3-class tumor segmentation** (necrotic core, enhancing tumor, edema) and **NSCLC vs. Breast Carcinoma** primary-origin classification. 
* 166 cases
* Licence: CC BY 4.0.

**Source:** Flouri D, Papanikas CP, Manikis GC, et al. *A longitudinal MRI dataset of brain metastases with tumor segmentations, clinical & radiomic data.* **Scientific Data**, 19 Nov 2025; 12:1828.

### Dataset 002 — MU_Glioma_Post
**Post-treatment glioma** multi-sequence MRI (t1c, t1n, t2f, t2w) with **4-class tumor segmentation** (NCR, ED, ET, NET_RC) and a **3-class primary diagnosis** label (GBM / Astrocytoma / Other). 591 timepoints from 203 patients (longitudinal).
**Source:** Mahmoud E, Gass J, Dhemesh Y, et al. *MU-Glioma Post: A comprehensive dataset of automated MR multi-sequence segmentation and clinical features.* **Scientific Data**, 20 Nov 2025; 12(1):1847.

### Dataset 003 — UCSD_PTGB
The **UCSD post-treatment glioblastoma** cohort imaged with T1post, FLAIR, and ADC. Provides **total cellular tumor** masks and **IDH mutation status** (wild-type vs. mutant). 184 cases, 3 channels.
**Source:** Gagnon L, Gupta D, Nguyen U, et al. *The University of California San Diego Post-Treatment Glioblastoma (UCSD-PTGBM) annotated multimodal MRI Dataset.* **Scientific Data**, 6 Jan 2026.

### Dataset 004 — PI-CAI
The largest dataset in the benchmark: **prostate MRI** (T2W, ADC, HBV) for **clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) segmentation** and **6-class ISUP grade** classification (Benign/Indolent + ISUP 1–5). 1,500 cases from 1,476 patients across 11 sites.
**Source:** Saha A, Bosma JS, Twilt JJ, et al. *Artificial intelligence and radiologists in prostate cancer detection on MRI (PI-CAI): an international, paired, non-inferiority, confirmatory study.* **Lancet Oncology**, 2024; 25:879–887.

### Dataset 005 — LUNA25
Cropped **low-dose chest CT patches** from the **LUNA25 challenge** for lung cancer screening. Each patch contains a nodule with a **segmentation mask** and a **benign vs. malignant** risk label. 6,141 nodule crops, single CT channel. Licence: CC BY 4.0.
**Source:** Peeters D, Obreja B, Antonissen N, Jacobs C. *Benchmarking of Artificial Intelligence and Radiologists for Lung Cancer Screening in CT: The LUNA25 Challenge.* **MICCAI 2025** (Zenodo: [10.5281/zenodo.15094631](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15094631)).

### Dataset 061 — PETWB_Lung
A subset of the **PETWB-REP** whole-body FDG PET/CT collection, paired with TotalSegmentator-derived **lung masks** and a **lung-cancer vs. other** label. 490 cases drawn from 4 cohorts, 2 channels (CT, PET). Tasks: binary lung segmentation + binary cancer-type classification. Licence: CC BY 4.0.
**Source:** Xue L, Feng G, Wenbo Z, et al. *PETWB-REP: A Multi-Cancer Whole-Body FDG PET/CT Dataset with Corresponding Radiology Reports.* **Scientific Data**, 2026.

### Dataset 062 — PETWB_Liver
Companion to Dataset 061 from the **same PETWB-REP source**, but targeting the **liver**: TotalSegmentator-derived liver masks paired with a **liver-cancer vs. other** label. 490 cases, 2 channels (CT, PET). Licence: CC BY 4.0.
**Source:** Xue L, Feng G, Wenbo Z, et al. *PETWB-REP: A Multi-Cancer Whole-Body FDG PET/CT Dataset with Corresponding Radiology Reports.* **Scientific Data**, 2026.

## 数据集

### 数据集 001 — BrainMets (PROTEAS)
**纵向多模态脑转移瘤**数据集，包含6个共配准通道（T1、T1c、T2、FLAIR、CT、RTP）。提供**3类肿瘤分割**（坏死核心、增强肿瘤、水肿）和**非小细胞肺癌 vs. 乳腺癌**原发灶分类。40名患者共166个时间点。许可证：CC BY 4.0。
**来源：** Flouri D, Papanikas CP, Manikis GC, 等。*A longitudinal MRI dataset of brain metastases with tumor segmentations, clinical & radiomic data.* **Scientific Data**, 2025年11月19日; 12:1828。

### 数据集 002 — MU_Glioma_Post
**治疗后胶质瘤**多序列MRI（t1c、t1n、t2f、t2w），包含**4类肿瘤分割**（NCR、ED、ET、NET_RC）和**3类原发诊断**标签（胶质母细胞瘤/星形细胞瘤/其他）。来自203名患者的591个纵向时间点。
**来源：** Mahmoud E, Gass J, Dhemesh Y, 等。*MU-Glioma Post: A comprehensive dataset of automated MR multi-sequence segmentation and clinical features.* **Scientific Data**, 2025年11月20日; 12(1):1847。

### 数据集 003 — UCSD_PTGB
**加州大学圣地亚哥分校治疗后胶质母细胞瘤**队列，采用T1post、FLAIR和ADC成像。提供**全细胞肿瘤**掩模和**IDH突变状态**（野生型 vs. 突变型）。184个病例，3个通道。
**来源：** Gagnon L, Gupta D, Nguyen U, 等。*The University of California San Diego Post-Treatment Glioblastoma (UCSD-PTGBM) annotated multimodal MRI Dataset.* **Scientific Data**, 2026年1月6日。

### 数据集 004 — PI-CAI
基准中最大的数据集：**前列腺MRI**（T2W、ADC、HBV），用于**临床显著性前列腺癌（csPCa）分割**和**6级ISUP分级**分类（良性/惰性 + ISUP 1–5）。来自11个中心的1,476名患者的1,500个病例。

### 数据集 005 — LUNA25
来自**LUNA25挑战赛**的裁剪**低剂量胸部CT图像块**，用于肺癌筛查。每个图像块包含一个结节及**分割掩模**和**良性 vs. 恶性**风险标签。6,141个结节裁剪图，单CT通道。许可证：CC BY 4.0。

**来源：** Xue L, Feng G, Wenbo Z, 等。*PETWB-REP: A Multi-Cancer Whole-Body FDG PET/CT Dataset with Corresponding Radiology Reports.* **Scientific Data**, 2026。

We give GPU memory consumption a 4GB tolerance, GPU Memory = max(0, Real GPU Memory-4096MB) because all the previous top teams (i.e., FLARE21-23) can achieve state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy within this tolerance. We also give running time a tolerance (the running time of the winning solution in FLARE 2023) because it satisfies the typical clinical requirements and the code has been publicly available. For each testing case, we compute the four metrics; Step 2. Rank participants for each of the N testing cases and each metric; Step 3. Average all these rankings. ## Common Questions

Please send emails to chingyuanyu.iec@gmail.com if you have any other questions. 

**Q:  How long can the participation request be approved after sending the signed challenge rule?**

A:  The request will be approved within 2-4 working days if the signed challenge rule document is filled out correctly.

**Q: I'm only interested in the challenge dataset but I do not want to join the challenge. Can I download the dataset without joining the challenge?**

A: Thanks for your interest. To ensure enough submissions, the dataset is only available to participants during the challenge. 

**Q: How many people can form a team？**

A: Each team can have at most 6 people. The authors in your paper should be the same as the team member list.

**Q: I have joined the challenge and downloaded the dataset. Can I quit the challenge?**

A: No! Please respect the signed agreement. If registered participants do not make successful submissions, all the team members will be listed in the dishonest list.

Algorithm-related issues

**Q: Can we use other datasets or pre-trained models to develop the segmentation algorithms?**

A: Yes, but you need to post them in the forum first. 

**Q: Can we manually annotate the unlabeled images to enlarge the training set?**

A: No. Any manual interventions are not allowed. 

**Q: Can we manually select the high-quality pseudo labels for the unlabeled images?**

A: No. Any manual interventions are not allowed. 

**Q: Does the validation submission affects the final ranking?**

A: No.

**Q: During the testing phase, can I modify the methods and the paper?**

A: Yes, you can make modifications before the testing submission. After making the testing submission, you cannot make modifications.


**Q: Can I use validation set for model pre-training?**
A: No!

**Q: Can I use other public datasets for model pre-training?** 
A: Yes, but you should post the dataset link on forum and also need to submit an algorithm that is trained only with the challenge dataset. 

**Q: When can I access the testing set?**
A: The testing set will not be released during the challenge to avoid data leakage.

# TwinWorld Challenge 2026

**TwinWorld Challenge 2026** is the official challenge of the [TwinWorld Workshop](https://twin-world.github.io/) at **ECCV 2026** (8 September 2026, Malmö, Sweden).

## Challenge Task

**Large-Scale 3D Semantic Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction**

The challenge targets large-scale drone imagery and semantic neural reconstruction on two datasets: **TUM** (TUM2TWIN) and **Gold Coast**. Participants are asked to:

1. **Novel view synthesis** — render photorealistic RGB images from the provided camera poses (all scenes).
2. **3D geometric reconstruction** — reconstruct a 3D point cloud of the scene (evaluated on TUM scenes).
3. **3D semantic segmentation** — assign one of 5 semantic class labels (ground, wall, roof, window, other) to each point of the reconstructed point cloud (evaluated on Gold Coast scenes).

## Timeline

| Milestone | Date |
|-----------|------|
| Development phase opens | 04 Aug 2026 |
| Final phase opens | 20 Aug 2026 |
| Final phase closes | 1 Sep 2026 |
| Results presented at workshop | 8 Sep 2026 |

## Workshop

The challenge results will be presented at the **TwinWorld @ ECCV 2026** workshop session (09:30, 8 Sep 2026).

The workshop focuses on scalable 3D and 4D scene understanding, multimodal reconstruction, semantic scene graphs, and real-world digital twin applications for autonomous driving, construction monitoring, and robotics.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

## Submission Format

Participants submit a **zip file** with the following structure (zip the dataset folders directly, without an extra top-level folder):

```
submission.zip
├── tum/
│   └── <scene_id>/
│       ├── rgb/
│       │   ├── <frame_id>.png      # rendered novel views, one per reference frame
│       │   └── ...
│       └── 3D_point_cloud/
│           └── point_cloud.ply     # x, y, z (float)
└── gold_coast/
    └── <scene_id>/
        ├── rgb/
        │   └── <frame_id>.png
        └── 3D_point_cloud/
            └── point_cloud.ply     # x, y, z (float) + classification (uchar)
```

- `rgb/` — rendered images, **PNG**, exactly the same resolution and frame IDs (file name stems) as the reference frames provided for each scene.
- `3D_point_cloud/point_cloud.ply` — the reconstructed point cloud. `x, y, z` are always required. The `classification` property (integer, one of the 5 class indices below or 255 = ignore) is required **only for Gold Coast scenes**.
- Scene IDs and frame IDs must **exactly match** those in the starting kit. A submission missing any required file is rejected without being scored (`incomplete_submission`).

## Semantic Classes (Gold Coast)

| Index | Class |
|-------|-------|
| 0 | ground |
| 1 | wall |
| 2 | roof |
| 3 | window |
| 4 | other |
| 255 | ignore (excluded from scoring) |

## Metrics

**2D rendering (all scenes):**

| Metric | Description | Direction |
|--------|-------------|-----------|
| **PSNR** | Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio on rendered RGB images | ↑ |
| **SSIM** | Structural Similarity Index (Wang et al., Gaussian-weighted) | ↑ |
| **LPIPS** | Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (VGG) | ↓ |

**3D geometry (TUM scenes only):** GT and submitted point clouds are cropped to the GT bounding box (+20 cm padding) and voxel-downsampled at 2 cm; then precision/recall **F-scores at 5 cm, 10 cm, and 20 cm** are computed. The reported `F-score` is the mean of the three.

**3D semantics (Gold Coast scenes only):** each GT point takes the label of the nearest submitted point within 10 cm (unmatched points count as errors). Per-class IoU is pooled over all scenes; **mIoU 3D** is the mean over the 5 classes.

## Final Score & Ranking

The leaderboard is ranked by **Final Score** (descending):

```
rendering_score = mean(PSNR / 50 capped at 1,  SSIM,  1 − LPIPS)   # in [0, 1]
geometry_score  = mean(F-score @ 5 cm, 10 cm, 20 cm)               # in [0, 1]
semantic_score  = mIoU 3D                                           # in [0, 1]

Final Score = rendering_score + geometry_score + semantic_score     # in [0, 3]
```

Higher is better; the maximum Final Score is **3.0**.

# 评估

## 提交格式

参赛者需提交一个 **zip 文件**，结构如下（直接压缩数据集文件夹，不包含额外的顶层文件夹）：

```
submission.zip
├── tum/
│   └── <scene_id>/
│       ├── rgb/
│       │   ├── <frame_id>.png      # 渲染的新视图，每个参考帧一张
│       │   └── ...
│       └── 3D_point_cloud/
│           └── point_cloud.ply     # x, y, z (float)
└── gold_coast/
    └── <scene_id>/
        ├── rgb/
        │   └── <frame_id>.png
        └── 3D_point_cloud/
            └── point_cloud.ply     # x, y, z (float) + classification (uchar)
```

- `rgb/` — 渲染的图像，**PNG 格式**，分辨率和帧 ID（文件名）必须与每个场景提供的参考帧完全相同。
- `3D_point_cloud/point_cloud.ply` — 重建的点云。`x, y, z` 始终需要。`classification` 属性（整数，为下面的 5 个类索引之一或 255 = 忽略）**仅对 Gold Coast 场景需要**。
- 场景 ID 和帧 ID 必须**完全匹配**起始工具包中的内容。提交缺少任何必需文件的结果将被拒绝，不计入评分（`incomplete_submission`）。

## 语义类别（Gold Coast）

| 索引 | 类别 |
|------|------|
| 0 | 地面 |
| 1 | 墙壁 |
| 2 | 屋顶 |
| 3 | 窗户 |
| 4 | 其他 |
| 255 | 忽略（排除在评分外） |

## 指标

**2D 渲染（所有场景）：**

| 指标 | 描述 | 方向 |
|------|------|------|
| **PSNR** | 渲染 RGB 图像的峰值信噪比 | ↑ |
| **SSIM** | 结构相似度指数（Wang 等人，高斯加权） | ↑ |
| **LPIPS** | 学习感知图像块相似度（VGG） | ↓ |

**3D 几何（仅 TUM 场景）：** 真实值点云和提交的点云都裁剪到真实值边界框（+20 厘米填充）并以 2 厘米体素下采样；然后计算精确度/召回率 **F-分数（5 厘米、10 厘米、20 厘米）**。报告的 `F-score` 是三个值的平均值。

**3D 语义（仅 Gold Coast 场景）：** 每个真实值点取最近的提交点（10 厘米内）的标签；未匹配的点计为错误。按类别计算 IoU 并在所有场景上汇总；**mIoU 3D** 是 5 个类别的平均值。

## 最终分数与排名

排行榜按 **Final Score**（最终分数）降序排列：

```
rendering_score = mean(PSNR / 50 上限为 1,  SSIM,  1 − LPIPS)   # 范围 [0, 1]
geometry_score  = mean(F-score @ 5 cm, 10 cm, 20 cm)            # 范围 [0, 1]
semantic_score  = mIoU 3D                                        # 范围 [0, 1]

Final Score = rendering_score + geometry_score + semantic_score  # 范围 [0, 3]
```

分数越高越好；最高最终分数为 **3.0**。

pages.title: Data
pages.content:
# Data

## Datasets

The challenge uses two large-scale drone imagery datasets:

- **TUM** ([TUM2TWIN](https://tum2t.win/)) — urban scenes; evaluated on **2D rendering + 3D geometry**.
- **Gold Coast** ([GT-LOD3 Benchmark](https://github.com/gdslab/GT-LOD3-Benchmark), [Gold Coast subset](https://stac.d2s.org/collections/ee10a5c0-2554-44e5-b59f-81eedfe02eb6?.language=en)) — coastal urban scenes; evaluated on **2D rendering + 3D semantic segmentation** (5 classes).

Full dataset access details are announced via the [TwinWorld Dataset website](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Zqlin/TwinWorld_Datasets).

## Starting Kit

The[ starting kit](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Zqlin/TwinWorld_Datasets/tree/main/starting_kit) is included with the dataset on Hugging Face, under `starting_kit/`. It contains:

- `README.md` — the submission format description, plus a set of reference Gaussian Splatting implementations to use as a starting point.
- `make_dummy_submission.py` — script that generates a correctly structured (random-content) submission zip for pipeline testing

## Submission Format

A single **zip file**, containing the dataset folders at the top level:

```
submission.zip
├── tum/<scene_id>/
│   ├── rgb/<frame_id>.png
│   └── 3D_point_cloud/point_cloud.ply         # x, y, z
└── gold_coast/<scene_id>/
    ├── rgb/<frame_id>.png
    └── 3D_point_cloud/point_cloud.ply         # x, y, z, classification
```

- Scene IDs and frame IDs (file name stems) must **exactly match** the reference frames provided for each phase.
- `rgb/` images must be PNG at exactly the reference resolution.
- Point clouds must be valid PLY with finite `x, y, z` coordinates. Binary little-endian PLY with `float32` coordinates is recommended to keep uploads small; store only the properties listed above (no colors/normals — they are ignored by the scorer and inflate the upload).
- Gold Coast point clouds additionally require an integer `classification` property with values in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 255}.

## Semantic Classes

5 evaluated classes: `0 ground, 1 wall, 2 roof, 3 window, 4 other`; `255` = ignore (excluded from scoring).

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# PBVS @ CVPR 2026 - Hyperspectral Images Super-Resolution (HISR) challenge

## Overview

Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution (HISR) goes beyond conventional SR: hyperspectral data contain rich wavelength-dependent information, where each band encodes material-specific spectral signatures. This means HISR must simultaneously preserve spatial detail and spectral integrity, ensuring reconstructed images remain physically meaningful rather than visually plausible only.

HSI data are also large and acquisition-intensive, making full-resolution capture costly and slow. Super-resolution therefore offers a powerful and practical pathway to reduce acquisition burden while enabling high-quality analysis.

This challenge introduces the **first** hyperspectral super-resolution benchmark within the PBVS CVPR 2026 workshop. It focuses on real LR-HR pairs, at ×4 SR under controlled lab conditions, using data collected with the same sensor and different optics to isolate spatial scaling while maintaining spectral consistency. 

**The challenge is to reconstruct ×4 real super-resolution hyperspectral images from the provided low-resolution hyperspectral patches image.**

Each low-resolution cube has a perfectly aligned high-resolution counterpart that serves as ground truth, enabling precise evaluation of both spatial recovery and spectral fidelity.
Participants develop methods that upscale the LR data by x4 while preserving spectral consistency across all wavelengths.


## Important dates

- 2026.01.12 Release of train and validation dataset (input and output)
- **2026.01.15 Test data release (inputs only)**
- 2026.01.15 Testing phase server online

- **2026.03.01 Test output results submission deadline**

# PBVS @ CVPR 2026 - 高光谱图像超分辨率（HISR）挑战赛

## 概述

高光谱图像超分辨率（HISR）超越了传统超分辨率的范畴：高光谱数据包含丰富的波长相关信息，每个波段编码特定材料的光谱特征。这意味着HISR必须同时保持空间细节和光谱完整性，确保重建的图像在物理意义上仍然有效，而不仅仅是视觉上可信。

高光谱图像数据量大且获取成本高，全分辨率采集成本昂贵且耗时。因此，超分辨率提供了一条强大而实用的途径来降低采集负担，同时实现高质量的分析。

本挑战赛引入了**首个**PBVS CVPR 2026研讨会内的高光谱超分辨率基准。它专注于真实的低分辨率-高分辨率配对数据，采用×4超分辨率，在受控的实验室条件下进行，使用同一传感器和不同光学系统采集的数据，以隔离空间缩放并维持光谱一致性。

**本挑战赛的目标是从提供的低分辨率高光谱图像块重建×4实超分辨率高光谱图像。**

每个低分辨率立方体都有一个完美对齐的高分辨率对应物作为真值标签，这使得能够精确评估空间恢复和光谱保真度。

参与者需要开发方法，将低分辨率数据上采样4倍，同时保持所有波长间的光谱一致性。

- 2026.01.12 训练和验证数据集发布（输入和输出）

- **2026.03.06 挑战赛参赛作品论文提交截止日期**

pages.content:
# Dataset

## Description
The dataset used in this challenge is **Version 2 of the HSI Lens Dataset**, introduced in the PBVS CVPR 2025 paper:  
[Ulrichsen et al., *“A True Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution Dataset”](
https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025W/PBVS/html/Ulrichsen_A_True_Hyperspectral_Image_Super-Resolution_Dataset_CVPRW_2025_paper.html)

This dataset provides **perfectly aligned low- and high-resolution SWIR hyperspectral image pairs**, acquired using a single Specim FX17 line-scanning camera (900–1700 nm). Spatial resolution differences were generated purely through **lens swapping**, ensuring identical spectral content while isolating spatial resolution as the primary challenge.

- High-resolution images: **3172 × 640 px**, captured with a 12° lens  
- Low-resolution images: **793 × 160 px**, captured with a 38° lens  
- Focus ensured using automated focus metrics and verified with sub-pixel registration  

Scenes cover **spectrally rich and diverse SWIR materials**, including plastics, wood, electronics, metals, fabrics, corrosion, printed text, painted surfaces, and various industrial objects.

## Splits
The dataset includes **70 registered image pairs**, divided as follows:
- **55** pairs for training  
- **10** pairs for validation  
- **5** pairs reserved for testing (not released)

Participants receive LR–HR pairs for training and validation.  
For the **test set**, only LR inputs are provided; high-resolution ground truth remains withheld for fair evaluation.
The LR version of the test set patches can be downloaded here: https://filesender.belnet.be/?s=download&token=237989c4-8c1a-4bd8-b652-49e5dbd90778

## Availability
The dataset can be downloaded from the repository “Files” section or via:  
**Zenodo DOI:** https://zenodo.org/records/18171738

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation Metrics

Submissions are evaluated using **Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR)** and **Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM)**, computed on 20 random patches with a size of **200x200x224 (w x h x bands)** of the hidden hyperspectral test set. Rankings are based on the combined performance across these metrics.

The LR patches of the test dataset can be downloaded here: https://filesender.belnet.be/?s=download&token=237989c4-8c1a-4bd8-b652-49e5dbd90778

Both metrics are computed **per band and averaged** over the hyperspectral cube. 

## Evaluation Dataset
Evaluation is performed only on a fixed set of patches, not on the full images.

* **5 test scenes** are selected.
* From each scene, **6 patches are extracted.**
* Each patch has dimensions** 200 × 200 × 224** (height × width × spectral bands).

This results in a total of 30 evaluation patches (5 scenes × 6 patches).
**All metrics are computed exclusively on these 30 patches.**
Full-resolution test images are not used for evaluation.

## Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR)
PSNR measures the pixel-wise reconstruction fidelity between the super-resolved output and the high-resolution ground truth.  
Higher PSNR values indicate more accurate spatial reconstruction.


## Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM)
SAM quantifies the **spectral similarity** between reconstructed and ground-truth spectra at each pixel by measuring the angle between their spectral vectors.  
Lower SAM values indicate better preservation of material-relevant spectral signatures and higher physical plausibility.

Only low-resolution inputs are provided for the test phase; corresponding HR ground truth remains hidden and is used exclusively for evaluation.

## Reproducibility and code availability (mandatory)

To ensure transparency, fairness, and reproducibility, all participating teams are required to make their full source code publicly available, preferably via a GitHub repository.

The released code must include all components necessary to reproduce the reported results, including:
- Training and evaluation scripts
- Model architectures and configuration files
- Dataset loading and preprocessing steps
- Environment specifications (e.g., requirements.txt, environment.yml, or Docker files)
- Clear, step-by-step instructions to run the code end to end

**The challenge organizers will independently train and evaluate all submitted methods from scratch to verify the reported results.
This verification process will directly affect the final ranking.**

**Teams that fail to provide their source code**, or that do not include sufficient information to reproduce their results, **will be disqualified** from the challenge.

# 评估指标

提交的方案使用**峰值信噪比（PSNR）**和**光谱角制图仪（SAM）**进行评估，计算基于隐藏高光谱测试集中20个随机补丁，每个补丁大小为**200x200x224（宽x高x波段）**。排名基于这些指标的综合性能。

测试数据集的LR补丁可从以下地址下载：https://filesender.belnet.be/?s=download&token=********-****-****-****-************

两个指标均**逐波段计算，然后在高光谱立方体上取平均**。

## 评估数据集
评估仅在固定的补丁集上进行，不在完整图像上进行。

* **选择5个测试场景**
* 从每个场景中**提取6个补丁**
* 每个补丁的尺寸为**200 × 200 × 224**（高 × 宽 × 光谱波段）

共产生30个评估补丁（5个场景 × 6个补丁）。
**所有指标仅在这30个补丁上计算**。
完整分辨率测试图像不用于评估。

## 峰值信噪比（PSNR）
PSNR衡量超分辨率输出与高分辨率真实值之间的像素级重建保真度。
更高的PSNR值表示空间重建更准确。

## 光谱角制图仪（SAM）
SAM通过测量每个像素处重建光谱与真实光谱向量之间的角度，量化**光谱相似性**。
更低的SAM值表示对材料相关光谱特征的保留更好，物理可行性更高。

测试阶段仅提供低分辨率输入；对应的HR真实值保持隐藏，仅用于评估。

## 可重现性和代码可用性（强制性）

为确保透明度、公平性和可重现性，所有参赛队伍必须将完整源代码公开发布，最好通过GitHub存储库。

发布的代码必须包含重现报告结果所需的所有组件，包括：
- 训练和评估脚本
- 模型架构和配置文件
- 数据集加载和预处理步骤
- 环境规范（例如requirements.txt、environment.yml或Docker文件）
- 明确的端到端分步说明

**挑战赛组织者将从头独立训练和评估所有提交的方法，以验证报告的结果。
此验证过程将直接影响最终排名**。

# Mixed Signals: V2X Collaborative 3D Object Detection Challenge

Welcome! This competition runs on the [Mixed Signals](https://mixedsignalsdataset.cs.cornell.edu/) dataset (ICCV 2025). The task is collaborative 3D object detection: given the LiDAR point clouds for a frame from up to four agents (five LiDAR streams), predict 3D bounding boxes for three meta-classes.
Class idClassGrouped from (10 fine-grained classes)
1Vehiclecar, truck, emergency vehicle, bus, electric vehicle, trailer
2Bikemotorbike, bicycle, portable personal mobility
3Pedestrianpedestrian
The sensors see the scene from different positions, so you can choose to fuse their point clouds to fill occlusions and extend the range of detection beyond a single viewpoint. You may use any subset of the agents and any fusion strategy (early, intermediate, or late fusion, or a single-agent baseline). The only requirement is that predictions are expressed in the "top" ego frame and follow the submission format. pages.content:
# Evaluation & Submission

This page covers how to format a submission and how entries are scored. For the
task, dataset and timeline, see the Overview tab.

## Building predictions

Produce one detection file per evaluation frame, named after that frame's id.
The frame ids you must predict are listed in the starting kit
(`validation_frames.txt` for Development, `test_frames.txt` for Final). Each
line is one detection with nine fields:

```
# cls cx cy cz dx dy dz yaw score
1 12.34 -3.21 0.05 4.10 1.92 1.55 1.5708 0.97
```

* `cls` ∈ {1=Vehicle, 2=Bike, 3=Pedestrian}
* `cx cy cz`: box centre in metres, "top" ego frame
* `dx dy dz`: length, width, height in metres
* `yaw`: heading (rotation about +z) in radians
* `score`: confidence in [0, 1] (used for ranking detections)

Zip the per-frame files at the root of the archive and upload on the Submit tab.
The starting kit's `SUBMISSION_FORMAT.md` is the authoritative spec, with a
sample submission and a format-checker. Run the checker before you upload.

## Evaluation

We follow the official Mixed Signals / OpenCOOD evaluation protocol exactly,
so leaderboard numbers are directly comparable to the dataset paper.

### Metric

* Matching: Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) rotated-box IoU between predicted and
  ground-truth boxes (the z/height dimension is not used for matching, in line
  with the dataset benchmark).
* Average Precision (AP): VOC-2010 "all-points" interpolation, the area
  under the precision-recall curve (not the 11-point variant).
* Per class: AP is computed independently for vehicle, bike and
  pedestrian at IoU thresholds 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7.
* Matching rule: within each frame, detections are ranked by descending
  confidence and greedily matched to ground-truth boxes. Each ground-truth box
  can be matched at most once. Unmatched detections (or matches below the IoU
  threshold) are false positives.
* Evaluation range: boxes whose centre falls outside `x, y ∈ [-51.2, 51.2] m`
  are excluded from both predictions and ground truth before scoring.

### Ranking by mAP

The leaderboard is ranked by the headline mAP, the mean of the three per-class
operating points reported in the paper:

```
mAP = mean( Vehicle AP@0.5 , Bike AP@0.5 , Pedestrian AP@0.3 )
```

(Pedestrians are scored at the looser 0.3 IoU because the boxes are small.) The
leaderboard also reports Vehicle and Bike AP at IoU 0.5/0.7 and Pedestrian AP at
IoU 0.3/0.5, matching the published tables, but only mAP decides the ranking.
Ties on mAP are broken by the leaderboard columns left to right (starting with
Vehicle AP@0.5), then by submission time, so earlier submissions rank higher.

### Scoring program

The scoring program is open and downloadable from the Submit / Files
area. It depends only on `numpy` and implements the BEV IoU and VOC AP from
scratch, so you can run it locally against your own validation labels to
reproduce leaderboard scores exactly.

# 评估与提交

本页介绍如何格式化提交内容以及条目的评分方式。有关任务、数据集和时间表，请参阅"概览"选项卡。

## 构建预测

为每个评估帧生成一个检测文件，文件名以该帧的id命名。您需要预测的帧id列在起始工具包中（开发集使用`validation_frames.txt`，最终测试使用`test_frames.txt`）。每一行是一个检测，包含九个字段：

```
# cls cx cy cz dx dy dz yaw score
1 12.34 -3.21 0.05 4.10 1.92 1.55 1.5708 0.97
```

* `cls` ∈ {1=车辆, 2=自行车, 3=行人}
* `cx cy cz`：边界框中心，单位为米，"顶部"自车坐标系
* `dx dy dz`：长、宽、高，单位为米
* `yaw`：航向角（绕+z轴旋转），单位为弧度
* `score`：置信度 ∈ [0, 1]（用于排序检测）

将各帧文件压缩到存档根目录并在"提交"选项卡中上传。起始工具包中的`SUBMISSION_FORMAT.md`是权威规范，包含示例提交和格式检查器。上传前运行检查器。

## 评估

我们完全遵循官方Mixed Signals / OpenCOOD评估协议，因此排行榜数据可直接与数据集论文进行比较。

### 指标

* 匹配：预测框与真实框之间的鸟瞰图（BEV）旋转框交并比（IoU）（不使用z/高度维度用于匹配，与数据集基准一致）。
* 平均精度（AP）：VOC-2010"全点"插值法，精确率-召回率曲线下的面积（非11点变体）。
* 各类别：AP在IoU阈值0.3、0.5和0.7处分别针对车辆、自行车和行人独立计算。
* 匹配规则：在每一帧内，检测按置信度降序排列，并贪心地与真实框匹配。每个真实框最多只能匹配一次。不匹配的检测（或低于IoU阈值的匹配）为假正例。
* 评估范围：中心落在`x, y ∈ [-51.2, 51.2] m`范围外的边界框在评分前从预测和真实数据中排除。

### 按mAP排名

排行榜按标题mAP排名，即论文中报告的三个各类别操作点的平均值：

```
mAP = mean( 车辆 AP@0.5 , 自行车 AP@0.5 , 行人 AP@0.3 )
```

（行人使用较宽松的0.3 IoU评分，因为其边界框较小。）排行榜还报告车辆和自行车在IoU 0.5/0.7处的AP以及行人在IoU 0.3/0.5处的AP，与已发表的表格一致，但仅mAP决定排名。mAP的平局按排行榜列从左到右打破（从车辆AP@0.5开始），再按提交时间打破，因此较早的提交排名较高。

### 评分程序

评分程序是开源的，可从"提交/文件"区域下载。它仅依赖`numpy`，从零开始实现BEV IoU和VOC AP，因此您可以在本地针对您自己的验证标签运行它，以精确再现排行榜分数。

17265.description:
本比赛面向城市级建筑立面构件精细理解，采用City-Facade大规模三维点云数据集。

数据由车载移动激光扫描系统采集，覆盖厦门市多类典型城市街区，累计道路长度约60 km。数据包含墙面、窗户、门、屋顶、广告牌、空调外机、雨棚和阳台等细粒度建筑立面要素标注，并提供语义级与实例级标签。

参赛者需要识别测试点云中的独立建筑立面构件实例，并输出相应实例编号和语义类别。

比赛采用结果提交模式。参赛者在本地完成模型训练和推理，仅向Codabench提交预测结果，平台使用隐藏实例标签进行自动评分。
17265.description_zh:
This competition focuses on fine-grained understanding of urban-level building facade components, utilizing the City-Fac dataset.

The data is collected by vehicle-mounted mobile laser scanning systems, covering multiple types of typical urban street blocks in Xiamen, with a cumulative road length of approximately 60 km. The dataset includes fine-grained building facade element annotations such as walls, windows, doors, roofs, billboards, air conditioning units, canopies, and balconies, with both semantic-level and instance-level labels provided.

Participants need to identify independent building facade component instances in the test point cloud and output the corresponding semantic categories and instance numbers.

The competition adopts a result submission mode. Participants complete model training and inference locally and only submit prediction results to Codabench, where the platform automatically scores using hidden instance labels.

# **建筑物立面点云语义/实例分割**

## **Overview**

本赛道采用 City-Facade 城市建筑立面点云数据集，开展建筑立面点云语义分割与实例分割。

参赛者需要为测试集中的每个点预测语义类别，并进一步区分同一语义类别下不同建筑立面构件的实例编号。

City-Facade 数据由车载移动激光扫描系统采集，覆盖厦门市 6 类典型城市街区场景，累计道路长度约 60 km，包含约 2 亿个带标注点。

语义类别如下：

| **编号** | **英文类别**              | **中文类别** |
| -------- | ------------------------- | ------------ |
| 0        | Background / Unclassified | 背景或未分类 |
| 1        | Wall                      | 墙面         |
| 2        | Window                    | 窗户         |
| 3        | Door                      | 门           |
| 4        | Roof                      | 屋顶         |
| 5        | Advertisement             | 广告牌       |
| 6        | Air Conditioner           | 空调外机     |
| 7        | Rain Shed                 | 雨棚         |
| 8        | Balcony                   | 阳台         |

参赛流程：

1. 在训练数据集上开发三维点云语义分割与实例分割模型；
2. 使用训练完成的模型预测测试数据；
3. 为每个测试点生成语义标签和实例标签；
4. 按指定目录结构压缩预测结果；
5. 将结果上传至 Codabench；
6. 平台自动评测并更新排行榜。

数据集项目地址：

```text
https://github.com/Ting-Devin-Han/City-Facade
```

## **Evaluation**

主排名指标为综合得分：

```text
Score = 0.5 × mIoU + 0.5 × AP50
```

其中：

- mIoU 用于评价语义分割精度；
- AP50 用于评价实例分割精度。

辅助指标包括：

- mIoU
- OA
- 各类别 IoU
- AP
- AP25
- AP50

所有指标均为越高越好。

每支队伍每日最多提交 5 次。

若综合得分相同，建议依次按照 AP50、mIoU、AP25 和提交时间确定排名。

## **Submission Format**

参赛者须为测试集中的每个点提供语义标签和实例标签，并提交一个 ZIP 压缩包。

压缩包根目录必须包含`predictions/`文件夹：

```text
submission.zip
└── predictions/
    ├── CAR/
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000000.txt
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000001.txt
    │   └── ...
    ├── JMC/
    ├── SGS/
    ├── XHR/
    └── YWR/
```

目录名称和预测文件名称必须与测试数据保持一致。例如：

```text
test/JMC/JMC-1-013_000000.txt
predictions/JMC/JMC-1-013_000000.txt
```

每个预测 `.txt` 文件为 `N x 7` 数组，字段顺序固定为：

```text
X Y Z intensity instance_id semantic_label instance_score
```

其中：

- `N` 为点云点数；
- `X Y Z` 为三维坐标；
- `intensity` 为激光强度；
- `instance_id` 为预测实例编号；
- `semantic_label` 为预测语义类别；
- `instance_score` 为预测实例置信度

字段索引从 `0` 开始时：

```text
X=0, Y=1, Z=2, intensity=3, instance_id=4, semantic_label=5, instance_score=6
```

提交文件必须满足：

1. 每个测试 `.txt` 文件都必须有对应预测文件；
2. 预测文件的相对路径和文件名必须与测试集一致；
3. 每个预测文件的点数必须与对应测试文件完全一致；
4. 点顺序必须与测试文件完全一致；
5. `X Y Z intensity` 四列应保持与测试文件一致；
6. `semantic_label` 必须为整数，取值范围为 `0` 到 `8`；
7. `instance_id` 必须为非负整数；
8. `instance_score` 必须是 `[0,1]` 范围内的有限数值，不允许使用 `NaN` 或正负无穷。
9. 对于语义类别 `1` 到 `8` 的前景构件，不同实例应使用不同的实例编号；
10. 对于类别 `0` 的背景或未分类点，`instance_id` 可设为 `0`；
11. ZIP 根目录必须包含 `predictions/` 文件夹，不要额外嵌套一层目录。

## **Citation**

使用 City-Facade 数据集开展研究或发表成果时，请引用：

```bibtex

  title={City-Facade: A city-level large-scale point cloud building facade dataset for semantic \& instance segmentation},
  author={Chen, Yiping and Li, Jonathan and Han, Ting and Feng, Huifang and Chen, Jun and Wang, Cheng},
  journal={ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing},
  volume={232},
  pages={675--688},
  year={2026},
  doi={10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2026.01.003}
}
```

# **Building Facade Point Cloud Semantic/Instance Segmentation**

## **Overview**

This track uses the City-Facade dataset to conduct semantic segmentation and instance segmentation of building facade point clouds.

Participants need to predict semantic categories for each point in the test set and further distinguish instance numbers of different building facade components within the same semantic category.

The City-Facade dataset is collected by vehicle-mounted mobile laser scanning systems, covering 6 typical urban street scene categories in Xiamen City, with a total road length of approximately 60 km and containing approximately 200 million annotated points.

Semantic categories are as follows:

| **ID** | **English Category**      | **Chinese Category** |
| ------ | ------------------------- | -------------------- |
| 0      | Background / Unclassified | Background/Unclassified |
| 1      | Wall                      | Wall                 |
| 2      | Window                    | Window               |
| 3      | Door                      | Door                 |
| 4      | Roof                      | Roof                 |
| 5      | Advertisement             | Advertisement Board  |
| 6      | Air Conditioner           | Air Conditioner Unit |
| 7      | Rain Shed                 | Rain Shed            |
| 8      | Balcony                   | Balcony              |

Competition workflow:

1. Develop 3D point cloud semantic and instance segmentation models on the training dataset;
2. Use the trained model to predict test data;
3. Generate semantic labels and instance labels for each test point;
4. Compress prediction results according to the specified directory structure;
5. Upload results to Codabench;
6. The platform automatically evaluates and updates the leaderboard.

Dataset project address:

```text
https://github.com/gorgeouseping/City-Facade
```

## **Evaluation**

The main ranking metric is the comprehensive score:

```text
Score = 0.5 × mIoU + 0.5 × AP50
```

Where:

- mIoU is used to evaluate semantic segmentation accuracy;
- AP50 is used to evaluate instance segmentation accuracy.

Auxiliary metrics include:

- mIoU
- OA
- IoU for each category
- AP
- AP25
- AP50

All metrics are higher the better.

Each team can submit a maximum of 5 times per day.

If the comprehensive score is the same, it is recommended to determine rankings in order by AP50, mIoU, AP25, and submission time.

## **Submission Format**

Participants must provide semantic labels and instance labels for each point in the test set and submit a ZIP compressed package.

```text
submission.zip
└── predictions/
    ├── CAR/
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000000.txt
    │   ├── CAR-30-003_000001.txt
    │   └── ...
    ├── JMC/
    ├── SGS/
    └── ...
```

Directory names and prediction file names must be consistent with the test data.

Each TXT file contains 6 fields:

```text
X Y Z intensity semantic_label instance_id
```

Array dimensions are:

```text
N × 6
```

Where:

- `N` is the number of points in the point cloud;
- `X Y Z` are 3D coordinates;
- `intensity` is laser intensity;
- `semantic_label` is the predicted semantic category;
- `instance_id` is the predicted instance number.

Submitted files must satisfy:

1. The number and order of points are completely consistent with the original test files;
2. The 3D coordinates and intensity fields must not be modified;
3. Semantic category ID range is 0-8;
4. Instance IDs must be non-negative integers;
5. Different instances use different instance IDs;
6. Prediction file directories and file names must be consistent with the test set;
7. The ZIP root directory must contain a `predictions` folder.

17680.description_zh: 欢迎来到首届"重演化身视频中远程操作者身份验证"国际竞赛。本竞赛将与[ACCV2026](https://https://accv2026.org/)联合举办。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
Welcome to the first International Competition on **Teleoperator Identity Verification in Reenacted Avatar Videos (Who Is Behind the Avatar?)— WBA2026 @ ACCV, Osaka, Japan**. ## Motivation Photorealistic avatars are increasingly used in telepresence, mixed reality, gaming, virtual environments, and AI-mediated video communication. In these settings, the visible face may be synthetic or may differ entirely from the person controlling it. Consequently, conventional face-recognition methods may not be sufficient to verify the identity of the underlying user. The **WBA** competition investigates whether behavioral information preserved in avatar videos can be used to authenticate the human teleoperator independently of the avatar’s visual appearance. Unlike conventional DeepFake-detection challenges, **WBA** does not ask participants to determine whether a video is real or synthetic. Avatar-generated videos are treated as legitimate communication media. The objective is instead to verify **operator authenticity**: whether an avatar is controlled by the authorized person. ## Challenge Task
**WBA** is a **cross-avatar teleoperator verification challenge**. For each verification trial, participants are provided with: * A gallery avatar video driven by a known teleoperator * A probe avatar video driven by an unknown teleoperator. Participants must determine whether the two avatar videos are driven by: * **Same teleoperator**, representing a genuine trial * **Different teleoperators**, representing an Imposter trial The gallery and probe videos may represent the same person through different avatar identities. Therefore, systems should focus on teleoperator-specific behavioral information rather than the visible appearance of the avatar. Potential behavioral cues include: * facial-motion dynamics * head movement and pose * expression timing * gaze behavior * speech-related facial movement * temporal motion patterns * other person-specific behavioral characteristics Participants may develop systems using RGB video, facial landmarks, head-pose features, expression dynamics, temporal motion descriptors, video embeddings, or other suitable representations. ## Dataset The source driving videos were collected in Japan during controlled dyadic online first-meeting conversations. The selected sequences are taken from the self-introduction portion of the conversations and include both speaking and listening segments. The original recordings were captured under controlled frontal-camera and lighting conditions. However, the original human videos are retained by the organizers and are not released to challenge participants. Instead, the motion and expression information from the original recordings are transferred to photorealistic avatar templates through a face-reenactment pipeline. The avatar appearances are selected from the publicly available **NVFAIR** dataset. This design reduces the direct exposure of the original participants’ visual identities while preserving motion and behavioral information relevant to teleoperator verification.
pages.content_zh: 欢迎来到首届**重演头像视频中的远程操作者身份验证国际竞赛——WBA 2026**。 ## 动机 超逼真头像越来越多地被应用于远程呈现、混合现实、游戏、虚拟环境和人工智能中介的视频通信。在这些应用中，可见的面孔可能是合成的，或者可能与控制它的人完全不同。因此，传统的面部识别方法可能不足以验证底层用户的身份。 **谁在头像后面？(WBA)** 挑战赛调查了头像视频中保留的行为信息是否可以用于独立于头像视觉外观的人类远程操作者身份认证。 与传统的深伪检测挑战不同，WBA不要求参与者判断视频是否真实或合成。头像生成的视频被视为合法的通信媒介。目标是验证**操作者的真实性**：头像是否由授权人员控制。 ## 挑战任务 WBA 2026是一项**跨头像远程操作者验证挑战**。 对于每次验证试验，参与者获得： 1. 由已知远程操作者驱动的图库头像视频；以及 2. 由未知远程操作者驱动的探针头像视频。 参与者必须确定这两个头像视频是否由以下任一情况驱动： * **相同的远程操作者**，代表真实试验；或 * **不同的远程操作者**，代表冒充试验。 图库和探针视频可能通过不同的头像身份代表同一个人。因此，系统应专注于远程操作者特定的行为信息，而不是头像的可见外观。 潜在的行为线索包括： * 面部运动动态 * 头部运动和姿态 * 表情时序 * 注视行为 * 与语音相关的面部运动 * 时间运动模式 * 其他人员特定的行为特征 参与者可以使用RGB视频、面部特征点、头部姿态特征、表情动态、时间运动描述符、视频嵌入或其他合适的表示方法开发系统。 ## 数据集 源驱动视频是在日本进行的受控二人组在线首次会面对话期间收集的。所选序列取自对话的自我介绍部分，包括说话和聆听片段。 原始录制是在受控的正面摄像头和照明条件下捕获的。但是，原始人类视频由组织者保留，不会向挑战参与者发布。 相反，来自原始录制的运动和表情信息通过人脸重演管道转移到超逼真头像模板。头像外观选自公开可用的 **NVFAIR** 数据集，而重演视频使用 **GAGAvatar** 生成。 这种设计减少了原始参与者视觉身份的直接暴露，同时保留了与远程操作者验证相关的运动和行为信息。 所发布的数据集中不包含音频，评估期间也不使用音频。
